title: Testing GitHub Copilot Knowledge Engineering: What Actually Works and What Doesn\’t
summary: GitHub Copilot's effectiveness for Business Central development improves significantly with domain-specific knowledge engineering, but the approach matters more than the amount of knowledge. A five-tier testing framework comparing generic programming knowledge, community documentation, atomic knowledge patterns, and Model Context Protocol delivery showed that systematic, context-aware knowledge delivery achieved 100x+ performance improvements consistently, while generic knowledge actually hurt optimization decisions.
key_points: Generic programming knowledge made Copilot suggestions worse for Business Central by creating confusion with domain-specific patterns
Atomic, focused knowledge delivered systematically (Tier 4 with MCP) achieved 100x+ performance improvements in six of nine modules, far outperforming static documentation approaches
Knowledge engineering effectiveness depends more on structured delivery and specificity than total knowledge volume
AI assistants need knowledge about when NOT to optimize as much as when to optimize, requiring false-positive testing
